jp: 母[はは]{は/が|wa-topic}毎朝[まいあさ]六時[ろくじ]{に|ni-time}起[お]きます。
en: My mother gets up at six every morning.
why: A clock time you can point to takes に.

jp: 父[ちち]{は/が|wa-topic}七時半[しちじはん]{に|ni-time}家[いえ]{を|o-departure}出[で]ます。
en: My father leaves the house at seven thirty.
why: The place you leave, with a verb like 出る, is marked by を.

jp: 妹[いもうと]{は/が|wa-topic}バス{で|de-means}学校[がっこう]{に/へ|ni-destination}行[い]きます。
en: My younger sister goes to school by bus.
why: A vehicle or means of travel takes で.

jp: 私[わたし]{は|wa-topic}台所[だいどころ]{で|de-place}朝[あさ]ご飯[はん]{を|o-object}作[つく]ります。
en: I make breakfast in the kitchen.
why: The place where an action is carried out takes で.

jp: 猫[ねこ]{は/が|wa-topic}ソファー{の|no-possessive}上[うえ]{に|ni-location}います。
en: The cat is on the sofa.
why: の links the sofa to its top, a noun that modifies the next noun.

jp: 部屋[へや]{に|ni-location}大[おお]きい本棚[ほんだな]{が|ga-existence}あります。
en: There is a big bookshelf in the room.
why: The thing whose existence is stated with あります is marked by が.

jp: 姉[あね]{は/が|wa-topic}料理[りょうり]{が|ga-stative}上手[じょうず]です。
en: My older sister is good at cooking.
why: The skill in 上手 is marked by が, not を.

jp: 弟[おとうと]{は/が|wa-topic}サッカー{が|ga-stative}好[す]きです。
en: My younger brother likes soccer.
why: The thing liked with 好き is marked by が.

jp: 夜[よる]、家族[かぞく]{と|to-with}晩[ばん]ご飯[はん]{を|o-object}食[た]べます。
en: In the evening I eat dinner together with my family.
why: A companion who does the action with you is marked by と.

jp: 母[はは]{に|ni-recipient}誕生日[たんじょうび]{の|no-possessive}プレゼント{を|o-object}あげました。
en: I gave my mother a birthday present.
why: The person who receives something you give takes に.

jp: 兄[あに]{に|ni-target}電話[でんわ]{を|o-object}かけました。
en: I phoned my older brother.
why: The person you direct a call at is the target and takes に.

jp: 毎朝[まいあさ]、犬[いぬ]{と|to-with}小[ちい]さい橋[はし]{を|o-path}渡[わた]ります。
en: Every morning I cross a small bridge with my dog.
why: A bridge you cross is a path you pass along, so it takes を.

jp: 私[わたし]{は|wa-topic}日曜日[にちようび]{に|ni-time}、父[ちち]{と|to-with}買[か]い物[もの]{に|ni-purpose}行[い]きます。
en: On Sundays I go shopping with my father.
why: The purpose of going, expressed with a noun like 買い物, takes に.

jp: 今日[きょう]{は|wa-topic}雨[あめ]{で|de-cause}洗濯[せんたく]{を|o-object}しませんでした。
en: Because of the rain I did not do the laundry today.
why: The cause of an outcome, here the rain, is marked by で.

jp: 母[はは]{の|no-possessive}料理[りょうり]{は|wa-topic}とてもおいしいです。
en: My mother's cooking is very delicious.
why: の joins the owner or maker, 母, to the noun 料理.

jp: 弟[おとうと]{は/が|wa-topic}肉[にく]{も|mo-both}魚[さかな]{も|mo-both}好[す]きです。
en: My younger brother likes both meat and fish.
why: Repeating も after each noun gives 'both A and B'.

jp: 姉[あね]{は/が|wa-topic}ケーキ{を|o-object}三[みっ]つ{も|mo-emphasis}食[た]べました。
en: My older sister ate as many as three cakes.
why: も after an amount stresses that it is a lot.

jp: 家[いえ]{に|ni-location}牛乳[ぎゅうにゅう]{が/は|ga-existence}ありません。
en: There is no milk at home.
why: The thing that exists or does not exist with ある is marked by が.

jp: 私[わたし]{の|no-possessive}部屋[へや]{は|wa-topic}二階[にかい]{に|ni-location}あります。
en: My room is on the second floor.
why: Where something is located, with あります, is marked by に.

jp: トイレ{は|wa-topic}どこ{に|ni-location}あります{か|ka-question}。
en: Where is the toilet?
why: The place where something exists, with ある, takes に.

jp: 昨日[きのう]{は|wa-topic}何時[なんじ]{に|ni-time}寝[ね]ました{か|ka-question}。
en: What time did you go to bed yesterday?
why: A specific time of day, even when asked about with 何時, takes に.

jp: 毎晩[まいばん]、お風呂[ふろ]{に|ni-destination}入[はい]ります。
en: Every night I take a bath.
why: 入る takes the place you enter with に.

jp: 家[いえ]{の|no-possessive}近[ちか]く{に|ni-location}スーパー{が|ga-existence}あります。
en: There is a supermarket near my house.
why: A thing's existence at a place, with ある, takes に.

jp: 母[はは]{と|to-with}電話[でんわ]{で|de-means}話[はな]しました。
en: I talked with my mother by phone.
why: A tool or medium of communication takes で.

jp: 兄[あに]{は/が|wa-topic}自分[じぶん]{の|no-possessive}部屋[へや]{で|de-place}勉強[べんきょう]{を|o-object}しています。
en: My older brother is studying in his own room.
why: The place where an activity such as studying happens takes で.

jp: 母[はは]{は|wa-topic}毎日[まいにち]スーパー{で|de-place}野菜[やさい]{を|o-object}買[か]います。
en: My mother buys vegetables at the supermarket every day.
why: The place where you do the buying takes で.

jp: 私[わたし]{は|wa-topic}ペン{で|de-means}手紙[てがみ]{を|o-object}書[か]きます。
en: I write letters with a pen.
why: The instrument you use to do something takes で.

jp: 朝[あさ]ご飯[はん]{は|wa-topic}パン{と|to-and}卵[たまご]{を|o-object}食[た]べます。
en: For breakfast I eat bread and eggs.
why: と links two nouns in a complete list: bread and eggs.

jp: かばん{の|no-possessive}中[なか]{に|ni-location}辞書[じしょ]{と|to-and}ノート{が|ga-existence}あります。
en: There are a dictionary and a notebook in the bag.
why: と joins two nouns that are both the subject of あります.

jp: 兄[あに]{は|wa-topic}父[ちち]{より|yori-comparison}早[はや]く起[お]きます。
en: My older brother gets up earlier than my father.
why: The standard of comparison with 'more than' is marked by より.

jp: 家[いえ]{から|kara-from}駅[えき]{まで|made-until}十分[じっぷん]かかります。
en: It takes ten minutes from my house to the station.
why: The starting point of a distance is marked by から.

jp: 毎晩[まいばん]、母[はは]{は|wa-topic}十一時[じゅういちじ]{まで|made-until}起[お]きています。
en: Every night my mother stays up until eleven.
why: まで marks the point in time up to which a state continues.

jp: 授業[じゅぎょう]{は|wa-topic}九時[くじ]{から|kara-from}です。
en: The class starts at nine.
why: The point in time when something starts is marked by から.

jp: 昨日[きのう]、母[はは]{と|to-with}デパート{に/へ|ni-destination}行[い]きました。
en: Yesterday I went to the department store with my mother.
why: The place you go to takes に (or へ).

jp: 母[はは]{は|wa-topic}私[わたし]{に|ni-recipient}この本[ほん]{を|o-object}くれました。
en: My mother gave me this book.
why: The receiver of something given to you takes に.

jp: 弟[おとうと]{は/が|wa-topic}犬[いぬ]{に|ni-recipient}ご飯[はん]{を|o-object}やりました。
en: My younger brother fed the dog.
why: The one who receives the food being given takes に.

jp: 誰[だれ]{が|ga-question}お風呂[ふろ]{を|o-object}掃除[そうじ]しました{か|ka-question}。
en: Who cleaned the bathroom?
why: A question word that is the subject is never marked with は; the unknown doer takes が.

jp: 兄[あに]{か|ka-or}姉[あね]{が|ga-subject}迎[むか]え{に|ni-purpose}来[き]ます。
en: Either my older brother or my older sister will come to pick me up.
why: か offers a choice between two options, one of which will happen.

jp: 日曜日[にちようび]{は|wa-topic}公園[こうえん]{か|ka-or}図書館[としょかん]{に/へ|ni-destination}出[で]かけます。
en: On Sundays I go out to either the park or the library.
why: か links two alternatives, 'the park or the library'.

jp: 母[はは]{は|wa-topic}「もうすぐ帰[かえ]ります」{と|to-quote}言[い]いました。
en: My mother said, "I'll be home soon."
why: The words that someone said are marked by と.

jp: 母[はは]{は|wa-topic}料理[りょうり]{を|o-object}する{の|no-nominalizer}{が/は|ga-stative}好[す]きです。
en: My mother likes cooking.
why: の turns the verb phrase 'to cook' into a noun that can take が.

jp: 妹[いもうと]{は/が|wa-topic}絵[え]{を|o-object}かく{の|no-nominalizer}{が|ga-stative}上手[じょうず]です。
en: My younger sister is good at drawing pictures.
why: の turns 'drawing pictures' into a noun that 上手 can describe.

jp: この傘[かさ]{は|wa-topic}母[はは]{の|no-pronoun}です。
en: This umbrella is my mother's.
why: の replaces the noun already known: 'my mother's (umbrella)'.

jp: どの靴[くつ]{が|ga-question}姉[あね]{の|no-pronoun}です{か|ka-question}。
en: Which shoes are my older sister's?
why: の stands for 'shoes' and means 'my sister's (pair)'.

jp: 今日[きょう]{は|wa-topic}いい天気[てんき]です{ね|ne-agreement}。
en: It's nice weather today, isn't it?
why: ね at the end invites the listener to share your feeling.

jp: ほら、そこ{に|ni-location}猫[ねこ]{が|ga-existence}います{よ|yo-assertion}。
en: Look, there's a cat right there!
why: よ tells the listener something they may not know yet.

jp: 明日[あした]{は|wa-topic}日曜日[にちようび]です{よね|yone-confirm}。
en: Tomorrow is Sunday, right?
why: よね confirms something you believe is true.

jp: 窓[まど]{の|no-possessive}外[そと]{で|de-place}雨[あめ]{が|ga-subject}降[ふ]っています。
en: Rain is falling outside the window.
why: The thing that does the action, rain falling, is marked by が.

jp: 週[しゅう]{に|ni-frequency}二回[にかい]、家[いえ]{の|no-possessive}掃除[そうじ]{を|o-object}します。
en: I clean the house twice a week.
why: A rate such as 'twice per week' is marked by に.

jp: 一日[いちにち]{に|ni-frequency}三回[さんかい]、歯[は]{を|o-object}みがきます。
en: I brush my teeth three times a day.
why: A rate such as 'three times per day' is marked by に.

jp: 妹[いもうと]{は|wa-topic}来年[らいねん]十歳[じゅっさい]{に|ni-change}なります。
en: My younger sister will turn ten next year.
why: The state something becomes with なる is marked by に.

jp: 弟[おとうと]{も|mo-also}宿題[しゅくだい]{を|o-object}しました。
en: My younger brother did his homework too.
why: も adds a further person to what has already been said: 'also'.

jp: 今日[きょう]{は|wa-topic}誰[だれ]{も|mo-total-negation}家[いえ]{に|ni-location}いません。
en: Nobody is at home today.
why: A question word plus も with a negative verb means 'nobody'.

jp: 冷蔵庫[れいぞうこ]{に|ni-location}何[なに]{も|mo-total-negation}ありません。
en: There is nothing in the fridge.
why: 何 plus も with a negative verb means 'nothing at all'.

jp: 部屋[へや]{に|ni-location}誰[だれ]{か|ka-indefinite}います{か|ka-question}。
en: Is there someone in the room?
why: A question word plus か makes it indefinite: 'someone'.

jp: 机[つくえ]{の|no-possessive}上[うえ]{に|ni-location}本[ほん]{や|ya-list}ノート{が|ga-existence}あります。
en: On the desk there are books, notebooks and so on.
why: や lists a few examples from a longer, incomplete list.

jp: 弟[おとうと]{は|wa-topic}家族[かぞく]{で|de-scope}一番[いちばん]早[はや]く寝[ね]ます。
en: My younger brother goes to bed earliest in the family.
why: で marks the group within which a superlative holds.

jp: この机[つくえ]{は|wa-topic}木[き]{で|de-material}できています。
en: This desk is made of wood.
why: The material a thing is made of, still recognisable, takes で.

jp: 宿題[しゅくだい]{は|wa-topic}三十分[さんじゅっぷん]{で|de-time-limit}終[お]わりました。
en: I finished my homework in thirty minutes.
why: The amount of time it took to complete something is marked by で.

jp: 母[はは]{から/に|kara-source}プレゼント{を|o-object}もらいました。
en: I received a present from my mother.
why: The person you receive something from is marked by から (or に).

jp: 弟[おとうと]{は|wa-topic}父[ちち]{と|to-reciprocal}同[おな]じ時計[とけい]{を|o-object}使[つか]っています。
en: My younger brother uses the same watch as my father.
why: 同じ takes と for the thing it is the same as.

jp: 今日[きょう]{は|wa-topic}寒[さむ]い{から/ので|kara-because}、コート{を|o-object}着[き]ます。
en: Because it is cold today, I will wear a coat.
why: から after a plain clause gives the reason for what follows.

jp: 毎朝[まいあさ]、牛乳[ぎゅうにゅう]{を|o-object}飲[の]みます。
en: Every morning I drink milk.
why: The thing that is drunk is the object and takes を.

jp: 父[ちち]{は|wa-topic}毎晩[まいばん]八時[はちじ]{に|ni-time}家[いえ]{へ/に|e-direction}帰[かえ]ります。
en: My father returns home at eight every evening.
why: へ marks the direction of movement toward a place.

jp: おじいさん{は|wa-topic}毎朝[まいあさ]新聞[しんぶん]{を|o-object}読[よ]みます。
en: My grandfather reads the newspaper every morning.
why: The thing that is read is the object and takes を.

jp: 友達[ともだち]{に/へ|ni-recipient}手紙[てがみ]{を|o-object}書[か]きました。
en: I wrote a letter to my friend.
why: The person a letter is written to takes に.
